# Game model (peg solitaire variant)

- 10 levels. Progress advances when a level is solved.
- Board = grid of cells drawn as gray squares on white, surrounded by blue "water".
  Cell pitch ≈ 48 px in the 512x512 view (gray tile ≈33px, white gap ≈15px).
- Green circle = peg. Empty gray cell = hole.
- Goal: standard peg solitaire — jump a peg over an orthogonally adjacent peg into
  the empty cell directly beyond; jumped peg is removed. Solve = reduce to ONE peg.
  (Level 1 completed exactly when a single peg remained.)

## Controls
- ACTION6 (click) on a peg = select it; dark ring appears on it and gray "ghost"
  rings appear on every legal landing cell for that peg.
- ACTION6 on a ghost landing cell = perform the jump (animated, ~10 frames).
- ACTION1-4 (arrows) appear to do NOTHING (tested with and without a moved peg).
  Do not waste actions on them.
- ACTION7 = undo.
- Minimum cost = 2 actions per jump (select + land). N pegs => 2*(N-1) actions.

## Method
1. Read pixel samples to map grid cells (find cell centers, pitch 48).
2. List peg coordinates, solve peg-solitaire on paper (search backwards if needed).
3. Execute select/land click pairs.

## Notes
- Later levels have multiple disjoint board regions joined by black "pipe" lines,
  plus special tiles (e.g. an orange/yellow tile) — semantics TBD (likely a
  teleport/link so a jump can cross between regions).

# Game model — "peg solitaire with ferries"

10 levels. Level advances when the board reaches ONE peg total.

## Board
- Cells are gray tiles on white boards (raised, blue drop-shadow), surrounded by blue water.
- Grid pitch = 48 px in the 512x512 view (tile ~33px + ~15px gap). Cell centers lie on a
  global 48px lattice.
- Green circle = peg. A level may contain several disjoint boards.

## Core rule (peg solitaire)
- A peg jumps over an orthogonally ADJACENT peg into the empty cell directly beyond
  (2 cells away, straight line); the jumped peg is removed.
- Win = exactly one peg remains. If no legal move remains with >1 peg, the level FAILS
  (pegs turn gray, a purple restart button appears at bottom-left; click it to restart).
- Adjacency requires physical adjacency on the lattice — cells of different boards count
  as adjacent only when the boards are drawn touching/1 pitch apart.

## Orange tile = FERRY (key mechanic, introduced in level 2)
- A 1-cell movable platform, joined to boards by black cables.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 (up/down/left/right) MOVE THE FERRY, not pegs. They work with or without
  a selection (they clear any selection). Arrows never move pegs.
- The ferry can only move along its cable path (a fixed track between two dock points).
  A move perpendicular to the track does nothing (wasted action).
- The ferry's cell can hold a peg. Jumps to/from the ferry are legal ONLY when the ferry
  is docked, i.e. sitting on the lattice cell directly adjacent to the board's edge cell,
  in line with the jump. Cable connection alone is NOT enough.
- Ferry with a peg aboard can be driven to another dock; the peg rides along.

## Controls
- ACTION6 on a peg = select (dark ring) + gray ghost rings on every legal landing cell.
  A peg with no legal move just shakes (frame_count 3) and is not selected.
- ACTION6 on a ghost = execute the jump (~10 frames).
- ACTION7 = undo. No RESET action; restart = click the purple button after a fail.
- Top-left thin bar grows 8px per action = action counter (no observed limit).

## Method
1. Map cells with read_pixels (a 64x64 sample of the whole 512x512 view works well:
   each sample = 8px, one cell = 6 samples).
2. Identify the peg path; typical design: a path of 10 cells with pegs at positions
   1,2,4,6,8 solved by 4 forward jumps (1→3, 3→5, 5→7, 7→9).
3. Plan ferry docking BEFORE spending jumps; count arrow moves along the track.

# Game model — "peg solitaire with ferries"

10 levels. A level is won when exactly ONE peg remains anywhere.

## Board
- Cells = gray tiles on white boards (blue drop-shadow), in blue water. Lattice pitch 48 px.
- Green circle = peg. Boards can be irregular; several boards per level.
- If no legal move remains with >1 peg: FAIL (pegs gray out, purple restart button
  appears bottom-left; click it to restart the level).

## Core rule
- Peg jumps over an orthogonally ADJACENT peg into the empty cell directly beyond;
  jumped peg is removed. Physical adjacency on the lattice is required.

## Orange tile = FERRY
- 1-cell movable platform that can hold a peg; joined to boards by black cables.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 move ALL ferries simultaneously, each along its own cable track.
  A ferry that cannot move in that direction (track bends/ends) simply stays, so
  directions can address ferries semi-independently.
- Jumps to/from a ferry work only when the ferry sits on the lattice cell directly
  adjacent to the board edge cell (docked). Cable connection alone is not enough.
- A ferry carries its peg while moving.

## Camera
- The view is a 512x512 window on a possibly larger world. It SCROLLS to follow ferry
  movement (roughly keeping the moving ferry near screen center). Jumps don't scroll it.
- After any ferry move, re-establish the offset (find a known object, e.g. the ferry)
  before computing click coordinates: screen = world - offset.

## Controls
- ACTION6 on a peg = select (dark ring) + gray ghost rings on legal landings;
  a peg with no legal move shakes (frame_count 3) and is not selected.
- ACTION6 on a ghost = jump (~10 frames). ACTION7 = undo. No RESET action.
- Top-left bar = action counter (8px per action).

## Method
1. Map the world with read_pixels (64x64 sample of the full view = 8px/sample,
   one cell = 6 samples). Sample cell centers (rows/cols aligned to the lattice)
   to classify: gray=empty cell, green=peg, light blue=no cell.
2. Solve the peg-solitaire on paper first, including ferry docking positions and
   the number of arrow moves along each track.
3. Watch for off-screen parts: move a ferry to scroll and reveal them.

## Unknown elements
- Purple/magenta tiles (level 4): semantics TBD.

# Game model — "peg solitaire with ferries"

10 levels. A level is won when exactly ONE green peg remains.

## Board
- Cells = gray tiles on white boards (blue drop-shadow), in blue water. Lattice pitch 48 px.
- Green circle = peg. Levels contain several boards, often larger than the 512px view.
- If no legal move remains with >1 peg: FAIL (pegs gray out; a purple restart button
  appears bottom-left; click it to restart the level).

## Core rule
- A peg jumps over an orthogonally ADJACENT peg (or purple tile) into the empty cell
  directly beyond; a jumped PEG is removed, a jumped PURPLE TILE STAYS.
- Purple/magenta tiles are permanent, immovable bounce-posts: they let a single peg
  travel 2 cells at a time without losing pegs. Only peg-over-peg jumps reduce the count.

## Orange tile = FERRY
- 1-cell movable platform that can hold a peg; joined to boards by black cables (its track).
- ACTION1/2/3/4 move ALL ferries simultaneously, each along its own track; a ferry whose
  track doesn't continue in that direction stays put (so directions address ferries
  semi-independently).
- Jumps to/from a ferry require the ferry to sit on the lattice cell adjacent to the
  board cell, in line with the jump. A ferry can also serve as the LANDING cell of a jump
  over a purple tile (ferry-to-ferry hops), and pegs ride ferries.
- Purple ferry (level 5+): presumably a movable purple bounce-post — verify.

## Camera
- The 512x512 view scrolls to follow ferry movement (keeps the moving ferry near center).
  Jumps normally don't scroll, but a jump that ends the "action" near an edge can.
- After every ferry move, re-locate a known object to recompute screen = world - offset.

## Controls
- ACTION6 on a peg = select (dark ring) + gray ghost rings on legal landings; a peg with
  no legal move shakes (frame_count 3). ACTION6 on a ghost = jump. ACTION7 = undo.
- Top-left bar = action counter.

## Method
1. Map with read_pixels: sample cell centers on the lattice (gray=empty, green=peg,
   purple=post, orange/yellow=ferry, light blue=no cell).
2. Solve on paper: count pegs (n pegs need n-1 peg-over-peg jumps), plan ferry docks and
   track moves before spending actions.

# Game model — "peg solitaire with ferries"

10 levels. WIN = exactly ONE GREEN peg remains anywhere in the level.
FAIL = no legal jump exists while >1 green peg remains (pegs gray out, a purple restart
button appears bottom-left). ACTION7 (undo) UNDOES A FAIL — very useful for probing.

## Pieces
- GREEN peg: normal. Jumping over a green REMOVES it.
- PURPLE tile: fixed post. Jumpable, never removed, never moves.
- RED peg: mobile post. It can jump like a peg, BUT no piece is ever removed by a jump
  involving red (neither the red nor the peg it jumps over). A green and a red can
  leapfrog each other indefinitely -> use red as a portable stepping stone to walk a
  green peg across empty boards. Red does NOT count for the win condition.
- ORANGE FERRY: 1-cell movable platform on a black cable track; can hold a peg
  (also the red). Two ferries can sit side by side and separate at junctions.

## Rules
- A peg jumps over an orthogonally adjacent peg/post into the empty cell directly beyond.
- A ferry cell counts as a landing cell only when docked in line; an EMPTY ferry cannot be
  jumped over.
- Arrow keys move ALL ferries along their tracks simultaneously; a ferry whose track has no
  continuation in that direction stays. Ferries block each other on a track.

## Camera
- The 512x512 view scrolls only to follow a PEG (including a peg riding a ferry).
  Moving empty ferries does NOT scroll the view, so explore by carrying a peg.

## Method
1. Map with read_pixels (64x64 full-view sample = 8px/sample; 6 samples per cell).
2. Count green pegs: n greens need n-1 capturing jumps. Plan the ORDER so the survivor
   is never stranded (a peg with no adjacent post/peg is dead).
3. Probe unknown mechanics with a jump, then ACTION7 to undo if it fails.

## What went wrong before
Removing a green while the survivor has no adjacent post strands it -> fail. Order matters:
capture last with the peg that will survive.

toward G3). Ferries at x=30 and x=318 only run vertically, so a third ferry (off-screen)
probably serves x=414. Explore by riding a peg east.

I've completed **5 of the 10 levels** and built a solid, revisable model of this game. Here's the summary:

## Game model discovered (recorded in GUIDE.md)

**Core**: peg solitaire — a green peg jumps over an adjacent piece into the empty cell beyond; the level is won when exactly **one green peg** remains, and fails when no jump exists with >1 green.

**Pieces learned by experiment:**
| Piece | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Green peg | Normal; captured when jumped over |
| **Orange ferry** | 1‑cell platform on a black cable track; carries pegs; jumps to/from it require it to be **docked** in line with the jump |
| **Purple tile** | Permanent post — jumpable but never removed (lets one peg travel alone) |
| **Purple ferry** | A movable purple post |
| **Red peg** | Mobile post: it can jump, but **no piece is ever removed** in a red‑involved jump → a green and the red can leapfrog indefinitely, letting a lone peg cross empty boards |

**Controls/meta:** arrows move *all* ferries simultaneously along their tracks (so directions address ferries semi‑independently); the 512×512 view is a **camera that only follows pegs** (empty ferries don't scroll it, so exploration requires carrying a peg); **ACTION7 undoes even a FAIL**, which makes probing risky moves safe.

## Levels solved
1. **L1** – basic 10‑cell path (4 jumps).
2. **L2** – discovered the ferry: docked it against the board, rode the peg across.
3. **L3** – large scrolling level; solved a 10‑peg funnel using two ferries and a cable network.
4. **L4** – purple posts + three ferries, including ferry‑to‑ferry hops over a purple.
5. **L5** – purple ferry used as a portable post, plus careful ferry sequencing on a shared track.

## Level 6 (in progress)
A very large multi‑board level with a red peg. I cracked its central trick (green+red leapfrogging, and carrying **both** on the twin ferry), cleared the western board and one eastern peg, and left the level in a live (non‑failed) state with notes in WORKING.md: the remaining obstacle is finding the ferry that serves the dock at the arm's east end so the peg can reach the last three greens.

# Game model — "peg solitaire with ferries"

10 levels. WIN = exactly ONE GREEN peg remains in the level.
FAIL = no legal move while >1 green remains (pegs gray out, purple restart button appears).
ACTION7 (undo) undoes moves, including a FAIL — useful for probing.

## Pieces
- GREEN peg: jumping over a green REMOVES it. Only greens count for the win.
- PURPLE tile: fixed post. Jumpable, never removed, never moves. (Drawn with a black bar.)
- RED peg: mobile post. Moves like a peg but NOTHING is removed by a jump involving red
  (neither the red nor the piece it jumps). Portable stepping stone.
- ORANGE FERRY (yellow border): 1-cell platform on a black cable. May carry a peg OR a
  purple post ("purple ferry" = mobile post).
- BLUE pegs: seen first in level 8; behaviour unknown.

## Movement rules (confirmed)
- ONLY jumps: a piece jumps over an orthogonally adjacent piece into the empty cell 2 away.
  There are NO single-step moves (clicking a piece shows ghost markers for every legal
  landing; adjacent empty cells never show ghosts).
- A docked ferry counts as a normal cell: you may land on an EMPTY docked ferry, and you may
  jump OVER a piece (peg or purple) that is riding a docked ferry.
- An EMPTY ferry cannot be jumped over (nothing to jump).
- Click piece = select (shows ghosts), click ghost = move. 2 actions per jump.

## Ferries / cables
- Arrow keys move ALL ferries one cell simultaneously along their cables; a ferry with no
  cable in that direction stays; ferries block each other and push nothing.
- A cable's drawn end marks the last ferry cell: the ferry stops with its cell touching the
  end. Where a cable ends at a board edge, that last cell is a dock aligned with the board
  cells (ferry sits one cell outside the board).
- Junction x-positions on a horizontal cable with no vertical branch are safe parking spots
  (immune to Up/Down); positions on a vertical branch are immune to Left/Right; a cable's
  far end is immune to that direction.
- Separate cable networks exist; a ferry cannot cross between them.

## Camera
- The view scrolls only to follow a PEG (including a peg riding a ferry). Moving empty
  ferries never scrolls. Screen coords shift after scrolls — re-map after any scroll.

## Method
1. Map with read_pixels (64x64 full-view sample = 8px/sample; cells are 48px).
2. Identify every green; plan which single green survives and which jump removes the others.
3. Use red / purple-ferries as portable posts; use ferries to move pegs between boards.
4. Before a long ferry dance, simulate ALL ferries (they move together) on paper.

# Game model — "peg solitaire with ferries" (COMPLETED 10/10)

WIN a level = exactly ONE GREEN peg remains anywhere in the level (levels can hide extra
greens off-screen; if the level doesn't end after a capture, more greens exist elsewhere).
FAIL = no legal move remains while >1 green exists. ACTION7 undoes moves (incl. a FAIL).

## Pieces
- GREEN: the only piece ever removed, and only when a GREEN jumps over it.
- PURPLE tile: fixed post (drawn on a black bar). Never moves, never removed.
- RED / BLUE pegs: mobile posts. They move by jumping like pegs but are never removed, and
  they never remove what they jump (a blue/red jumping a green leaves the green in place).
- ORANGE FERRY (yellow border): 1-cell platform on a black cable; may carry a peg or a
  purple post. Ferries never enter board cells.

## Movement (strict)
- ONLY jumps: over an orthogonally adjacent piece into the empty cell two away. No steps.
- Click a piece to select (grey ghost markers = every legal landing), click a ghost to move.
  Selection is lost after each move: 2 actions per jump.
- A docked ferry is a normal cell: you may land on an empty one and jump over an occupied one.
  An empty ferry cannot be jumped over.
- INVARIANT: a jump changes one coordinate by 2, so every piece is locked to its
  (column parity, row parity) class. Use this first to decide which captures are possible;
  only a ferry ride can move a piece between classes.

## Ferries / cables
- Arrow keys move ALL ferries one cell at once; a ferry with no cable that way stays, and
  ferries block (but never push) each other. Plan whole-fleet moves on paper.
- Immunity tricks: a ferry on a vertical ignores LEFT/RIGHT; on a horizontal ignores UP/DOWN
  (unless a branch exists); at a cable end it ignores that direction. Junction columns with
  no branch are safe parking. Two ferries on one track can only swap via a side branch.
- Docks: a cable ending at a board edge (or filling a notch in it) puts the ferry cell
  adjacent/in-line with the board cell; boarding always needs a post to jump over.

## Camera
- The view follows the last-moved PEG only (a peg riding a ferry counts). Empty ferries and
  blues generally don't scroll it; drive a peg west/east to expose off-screen areas, and
  re-read screen coordinates after every scroll.

## Method that worked
1. read_pixels 64x64 over the full view; cells are 48 px; identify all pieces and cables.
2. List every capture geometry (both greens adjacent + empty landing beyond), filter by the
   parity invariant, then work backwards to the posts and ferry docks needed.
3. Use paired leapfrogging (green+post, or two blues) to walk pieces along a line; a piece
   can only turn a corner where another post of the right class exists.

- Only greens are removed, and only by a green jumper — blues/reds are permanent portable posts.
- Moves are strictly jumps, so every piece is locked to its (column parity, row parity) class; ferries are the only way to change class. Checking this first eliminated impossible plans immediately.
- Arrow keys move every ferry simultaneously, so ferry logistics are a fleet puzzle solved with immunity tricks (verticals ignore left/right, cable ends ignore that direction, no-branch columns are safe parking).
